prompts.prompt:
Create a very polished, sleek, shippable enterprise desktop application mockup for AdaptOps. Canvas 1600x1000, flat screenshot, no device/perspective, all content inside viewport. Keep approved Direction A: white, extremely pale cool-grey workspace, deep navy #102238 type, deep teal #086273 primary action, restrained mint and amber accents, subtle hairline borders, Inter-like font, generous 32px spacing, unusually clear hierarchy. No purple, gradients, glass, giant icons, stock illustrations, decorative charts, glowing objects or marketing website.
Use minimal accurate English text. Exactly these shared business facts are available: Demo Materials is a synthetic company with Lille, Central and South depots. Site A needs 8 ISO100 pallets on 23 Oct; an internally confirmed delivery-date change creates a risk. An emergency purchase costs €1,420 and covers A while protecting B. A Central stock transfer remains conditional. Additional customer demand is an opportunity to qualify, not a confirmed sale. Never invent any numerical counts, savings, revenue, margins, elapsed time, timestamps, forecasts, stock quantities beyond 8 or financial values beyond €1,420. No invented real incident or external supplier relationship.
The user should understand immediately: what changed, business impact, next decision. Put sources/calculations behind a small "Evidence & calculations" link. Do not crowd the home with technical notes, logs, version IDs, controls, disclaimers or repeated badges. At the bottom only, small legible "Design proposal · Synthetic business data". Approving is never labelled executed.
Common app shell: top "AdaptOps" logotype, workspace "Demo Materials", date "22 Oct 2026", user "Paul". Compact left rail with exactly six labels: "Overview" selected; "Needs decision"; "In progress"; "Completed"; "Watches"; "Company knowledge". Do not create other destinations or notification counts. Fonts approximately 36px main heading, 22px card title, 16px body, 12px meta. Use realistic and internally consistent controls. One dominant teal call to action exactly "Review response →". One secondary textual action "View company context". One compact opportunity exactly "Additional demand" with amber status "To qualify". No chat box or setup form. Preserve clarity and enterprise practicality.

Composition A, visibly labelled "A · Decision first" in a small pill at the upper right, outside the primary content. This composition is a focused decision desk.
Main headline "A delivery needs your decision." Small supporting line "Know the impact. Choose the next move."
Use an approximately 180px very light left sidebar. Main workspace has a spacious central primary case card taking two thirds of the content width, and a narrow quiet plan-summary column on the right. Very restrained borders, absolutely no card nesting mess.
Primary card: eyebrow "SUPPLY UPDATE", title "Protect Site A’s delivery", one concise line "8 ISO100 pallets needed on 23 Oct." Two compact outcome rows under a divider: "Site A" paired with a red "Delivery at risk" tag, "Site B" paired with a green "Reservation protected" tag. Tiny source line "Internal delivery confirmation" without extra disclaimer. The bottom contains the large teal "Review response →" button and one unobtrusive "Evidence & calculations" link.
The right column is titled "Proposed response". Large elegant number "€1,420" with label "Emergency purchase cost". Beneath, "Covers A. Preserves B." and muted secondary text "Transfer: conditional". Do not show green final completion or "purchased".
Below the primary case card and side summary, a single shallow full-width opportunity row with a small mint trend icon, heading "Additional demand", short phrase "Check compatible free stock before making an offer", amber "To qualify" chip, and an understated right arrow. Visually secondary to the delivery risk.
Below that row only a small "View company context" text link. Large breathing room. No repeated hero descriptions. Beautifully balanced clean enterprise UI.

Composition B, visibly labelled "B · Impact workspace" in a small pill at the upper right of the workspace. This composition is a calm, highly refined master-detail operational cockpit, with the sophisticated proportions and typographic precision of a best-in-class enterprise SaaS product. It must feel distinctly different from a giant single-case hero. Keep the font sizes disciplined and realistic, main heading around 32px, no oversized pitch typography.
Main heading exactly "Business impact", short subtitle "What changed. What to do next." Under it a very thin company context bar "Lille / Central / South" and far-right small text link "View company context".
Central workspace occupies the full remaining area and is split into a wide decision list (roughly 58%) and a right inspector (roughly 42%), separated by a very subtle vertical border. Large white background, no card nesting.
Left list header exactly "Needs attention". Two airy full-width rows only:
1 Selected row with a thin teal left indicator and barely tinted background. Small amber chip "Risk". Main bold title "Site A delivery". One line "8 ISO100 pallets · 23 Oct". Far right "Review ready". This is the selected dossier.
2 Unselected row with a mint opportunity icon. Bold title "Additional demand". One line "Check compatible free stock before an offer". Amber small chip "To qualify".
Below these, a quiet empty-space area with one small factual statement "Existing reservations stay in every calculation." Do not invent more cases, counts, companies or metrics.
Right inspector, elegantly spaced: small eyebrow "PROPOSED RESPONSE", heading "Secure supply. Protect commitments." Then a compact source line "Internal delivery confirmation". Below two horizontal impact rows, "Site A" / red "Delivery at risk", "Site B" / green "Reservation protected".
A separate financial line with 40px "€1,420" and smaller label "Emergency purchase cost". Below in small type "Transfer remains conditional". At the bottom a full-width primary button "Review response →" and understated link "Evidence & calculations".
Keep the whole inspector visibly a proposed plan rather than executed. Screen density lower than a trading terminal, higher than a pitch slide. No bottom banners, no giant gradient fields. Beautiful fine alignment, understated short separators, generous whitespace, clarity. Footer "Design proposal · Synthetic business data".

Composition C, visibly labelled "C · Company brief" in a small pill at upper right of the workspace. Genuinely different layout from both the single-case hero and master-detail workspace: a refined editorial daily business brief. It must look like a working product with a clear next action, not a slide or landing page.
Use the same compact navigation rail and top bar. Main heading approximately 32px "Your business brief." Short subtitle "The change, the impact, the next move." Under heading a calm small line "Demo Materials · Lille / Central / South".
The main white working surface is one beautifully spaced vertically flowing brief, with NO nested card grid. Thin short dividers separate three narrative sections. On the right a narrow sidebar column, around 280px, holds only company context and a short opportunity.
Main brief section 01: small grey eyebrow "WHAT CHANGED", bold readable heading "A supplier delivery date has moved." Tiny attribution "Internal confirmation". Body one short line "Site A needs 8 ISO100 pallets on 23 Oct."
Section 02: small grey eyebrow "BUSINESS IMPACT". Two horizontally aligned compact factual blocks separated by whitespace: "Site A" with red "Delivery at risk" and "Site B" with mint "Reservation protected". Do not put icons inside giant colored boxes.
Section 03: small grey eyebrow "PROPOSED NEXT MOVE". A slim very pale teal horizontal action surface with a small purchasing outline icon. Left heading "Emergency purchase", right exact value "€1,420", underneath label "Proposed cost". Below it the understated text "Transfer remains conditional". One clear strong primary button "Review response →" and small "Evidence & calculations" text link.
Right column: header "Company context", three lines "Sites & stock", "Orders & reservations", "Suppliers & customers", with discreet outline icons; text link "View company context". Below a thin divider, a mint small arrow icon and title "Additional demand". One sentence "Check compatible free stock before making an offer." Amber status "To qualify". No other sidebar content or badges.
Enough whitespace to breathe, but keep body compact and realistic rather than giant. Baselines align across columns. Very calm tactile enterprise design with typography doing the work. Footer "Design proposal · Synthetic business data".
